source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. FCH Common Options → SATA Configuration Options → SATA RAS Support: Enabled e. FCH Common Options → USB Configuration Options → USB ECC SMI Enable: Enabled 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listvalidusb 6. Run the USB RAM1 Error injection: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --usbsata --errortype usb --socket 0 --instance 1 --errortarget 1 6.1 The system will reset immediately. 6.2 When system boot into operating system again, check dmesg log. 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- RAM1~N Error: inject the USB RAM1~N Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'usb|fatal|error'; echo __USB_RAM1~N_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.purpose: Inject the specified USB RAM fault across the required RAM1~N targets, verify the intended corrected or reset behavior with target-specific durable evidence, and prove the USB controller, ports and attached devices recover.
required_package: Definition of USB RAM1~N and complete required controller/instance/target/port/device coverage
Full listvalidusb output and immutable physical mapping for socket0 instance1 target1 and any N targets
Vendor-correct one-line or continued command syntax and semantics of usbsata errortype usb
Decision on correctable Criteria versus immediate reset, including exact severity/source fields
Rationale for SATA RAS Support in USB coverage and USB ECC SMI behavior
Supported OS, timeouts, boot/input/storage/management-device recovery, aborts and restoration
test_case.test_command: Enumerate valid USB targets; map every reported RAM target to socket, controller, instance, errortarget, port and device; resolve severity/reset policy and command-line formatting; capture raw BIOS/log/device baselines; inject one approved target once under OOB capture; correlate fresh source fields and reset; validate controller/device recovery; repeat only for an approved coverage matrix with restoration between targets.

Inventory boot media, input devices, USB NIC/BMC dependencies and active storage before selecting a target
